name: Denafrips

family_claim.evidence: The whole range is a discrete resistor ladder; that is the maker's entire product proposition. Roon forum, on its DSD handling.

_refused: Read 2026-11-25 at https://www.denafrips.com/blank-2 - the live terms page, which the footer link labelled « Terms & Conditions » points to rather than to the /terms-and-conditions/… paths in the sitemap. SECTION 2: « You agree not to reproduce, duplicate, copy, sell, resell or exploit any portion of the Service, use of the Service, or access to the Service or any contact on the website/application through which the service is provided, without express written permission by us. » SECTION 12: « you are prohibited from using the site or its content: (a) for any unlawful purpose; [...] (i) to spam, phish, pharm, pretext, spider, crawl, or scrape » The preamble is site-wide and not store-scoped: « This website/application is operated by DENAFRIPS team. [...] These TERMS AND CONDITIONS apply to all users of the site, including without limitation users who are browsers, vendors, customers, merchants, and/ or contributors of content. [...] By accessing or using any part of the site, you agree to be bound by these TERMS AND CONDITIONS. » There IS a « SECTION 1 - ONLINE STORE TERMS », but it is one section of eighteen and carries no reuse clause, while the two prohibitions sit outside it under a preamble binding « browsers » and « any part of the site ». The product and /specs-* pages are on that same host. No copyright footer exists anywhere - searched for. robots.txt is permissive (« User-agent: * / Allow: / ») with no Content-Signal and no Claude group, which does not override a contractual prohibition. No product page, /specs-* page or manual PDF was opened.
_a_record_was_WITHDRAWN_for_this: database/devices/denafrips/generique held one claim, 002-plafonds-par-entree.json, carrying per-input ceilings for USB and I2S against a lower set for AES/EBU, coaxial and optical. It was REMOVED on 2026-11-25 when this refusal was recorded, and the verifier's own guard names the only two resolutions: withdraw the record, or withdraw the refusal with the evidence that lifts it. The clause is measured, so the first applies. TWO reasons, and the second stands on its own: the claim was `kind: import` sourced to « Denafrips manuals and reviews » with NO URL - and a manual is the maker's content however it was obtained, so the route does not lift the clause. The figures are not restated here; a register entry documents a decision and this brand forbids reproduction.
_and_the_withdrawn_claim_contained_an_AD: Worth recording apart from the refusal, because it is a defect this catalogue would have had to fix anyway. The claim's own source note ended: « Consistent for the Pontus II, Venus and Terminator; the figures for the first-generation Pontus were not found and are assumed to follow. » An assumption, written inside a claim, under a generic model that covers the whole range - so a reader resolving a first-generation Pontus would have received ceilings nobody read. By this catalogue's own rule an invented figure is a defect, and « assumed to follow » is that rule's own words turned inward. It was found by the reader sent to harvest this brand, in the file it happened to open - not by any guard, which is the uncomfortable part: nothing in the verifier looks for a source note that admits its own gap.
_it_can_be_lifted_and_the_prize_is_named: Conditioned on « express written permission by us », which Section 2 itself contemplates; contact support@denafrips.com. Near the top of the letter list, because the site is unusually rich: the sitemap lists per-model HTML specification pages (/specs-pontus, /specs-venus, /terminator-specs, /specs-terminator-plus, /specs-hestia, /specs-iris, /specs-gaia and some fifteen more), a parallel set of /download-* pages holding the manual PDFs, and - most valuable of all - /config-pontus, /config-venus, /config-terminator, /config-tplus, /config-ares-15th, /config-enyo and /config-i2s. On this range the OS/NOS selection is a DIP-switch matter, so those config pages are where the non-oversampling legend is stated, which is the single property this catalogue values most. The earlier note that this maker's pages were images was partly a wrong-page problem: the /specs-* pages are HTML.
_two_hosts_that_are_NOT_the_maker: The maker says so itself on its home page: « We would also like to clarify that www.denafrips.eu is not operated by Denafrips Audio and does not serve as an official European branch of our brand. » And vinshineaudio.com is the authorised distributor, not the maker - it was not used. Also noted so nobody mistakes them for the terms: the sitemap's /terms-and-conditions/intellectual-property-rights and /terms-and-conditions/terms-and-conditions are broken CMS pages rendering only CE certificate images, and « Intellectual Property Rights » on this site means product conformity, not copyright.
_what_the_withdrawal_COST_measured: Measured from the field registry before and after. Removing that one record dropped the count of SIX fields, four of them level 3 - the tier where this base has 0 complete records and where almost nothing is ever filled in: analog_filter 27 to 26, dsd_direct 27 to 26, pcm_dsd_level_offset_db 5 to 4, dsd_reconverted_to_pcm 7 to 6, plus correctable 71 to 70 and native_dsd 129 to 128. So one import-sourced claim with no URL was carrying a fifth of everything the base knows about PCM-to-DSD level offsets, and a twentieth of what it knows about analogue filters. That is the price of this refusal stated honestly, and it is also an argument about the letter: the makers who document what a device does INSIDE are rare, and this one did it in a manual while forbidding its reproduction.
